transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-15
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood CSM), Ethan Huang (Redwood SE), Dana Ellis (Aurora Head of ML), Priya Nair (Aurora Eng Manager), Carlos Gomez (Aurora Security), Maya Singh (Aurora DevOps), Jonas Lee (Aurora Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Kickoff for Aurora Health onboarding with Redwood; discuss deployment options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), security/compliance ask (SOC2, audit logs, KMS), pilot scope and next steps.

Topics: Onboarding timeline, Dedicated capacity trial, SSO/KMS, perf benchmarks, rollout plan, cost estimates.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie with Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Quick roundtable, uh, who we have with Aurora?
[00:00:15] Dana Ellis: Hi Jamie, Dana here, head of ML at Aurora.
[00:00:18] Priya Nair: Priya, engineering manager.
[00:00:20] Carlos Gomez: Carlos, security and compliance.
[00:00:22] Maya Singh: Maya, DevOps.
[00:00:25] Jonas Lee: Jonas from product.
[00:00:27] Sofia Martinez: Hi all, Sofia here, customer success, I'll coordinate onboarding and runbooks.
[00:00:32] Ethan Huang: Ethan, SE, I'll handle the technical side and benchmarks.
[00:00:35] Jamie Park: Awesome. Goal for today is to align on pilot scope, confirm security asks, and set next steps for a Dedicated trial + initial perf run. Should take 30-45. Sound good?
[00:00:47] Dana Ellis: Yup, that's perfect.

[00:02:10] Jamie Park: To start, quick background: Redwood gives a unified API and runtime for inference - hosted API for quick dev, Dedicated for committed capacity, and Private for VPC/on-prem. We'll tailor the pilot to what you want to validate, usually throughput/latency and integration patterns.
[00:02:35] Dana Ellis: Our primary concern is predictable latency for patient-facing features; we also need full auditability and keys managed by us. We're leaning toward Dedicated or Private but want to understand tradeoffs versus hosted.
[00:03:00] Ethan Huang: Totally. In practice Dedicated gets you predictable throughput and isolation, while Private gives you full network control and on-prem options. Hosted is fastest to start but doesn't meet your KMS or VPC constraints.
[00:03:18] Carlos Gomez: Yeah, for compliance we need customer-managed KMS, audit logs for model requests, and SSO integration. SOC2 report is required. Also data residency - US only.
[00:03:36] Jamie Park: Understood. We support KMS integrations (HSM-compatible), audit logs and regional hosting. We'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts. There may be a few redaction notes - the security pack covers what we can share.

[00:05:05] Priya Nair: On the engineering side we have an existing in-house model gateway and some edge caching; we want to see how Redwood's KV cache and batching would mesh with our proxy. Also curious about model versioning and rollouts - we do canary releases.
[00:05:30] Ethan Huang: Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching and smart batching; we also have rollouts and canary policies in the Console. We'll walk you through canary config - some of the naming in the docs is a little terse, apologies if the auto-transcript spells it weird - "red wood con-soul" sometimes.
[00:05:48] Dana Ellis: Haha noted, the transcript already is doing that.

[00:07:00] Jonas Lee: Timeline wise, we'd like a pilot live in two weeks and then a production decision in a month. Is that realistic?
[00:07:10] Sofia Martinez: It's tight but doable. For a pilot we usually need sample traffic + SSO info + a small set of eval prompts.
[00:07:22] Priya Nair: We can provide sample traffic and QPS profile. On SSO, we use Okta.
[00:07:30] Carlos Gomez: We'll also need an IP allowlist and a signed DPA before sensitive data flows.
[00:07:38] Jamie Park: Agree. We'll provide DPA template and add that to next steps. For the Dedicated trial we can provision a small GPU pool for you to run tests.

[00:09:05] Ethan Huang: Quick note on performance: what's your latency SLO for patient UX? 200-300 ms per request, or are you expecting lower?
[00:09:12] Dana Ellis: Ideally <200ms P95 for the short responses we're doing. For longer assistant-style messages it's okay to be slower but primary endpoints need snappy responses.
[00:09:25] Ethan Huang: Okay. The baseline depends a lot on model choice, sequence length, and batching. If you plan to run larger context windows we can show latency vs cost tradeoffs and quantization options.
[00:09:40] Dana Ellis: We're open to quantized variants if quality holds.

[00:11:10] Maya Singh: One ops question: how do you handle autoscaling and cold-starts for Dedicated? We need to avoid tail latency spikes.
[00:11:20] Ethan Huang: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity; runtime keeps KV cache warm if you configure a steady-state traffic target. There are knobs in the Console to tune batching windows and request routing. We'll share recommended policies.
[00:11:40] Maya Singh: Cool. We'd like the ability to pin model versions and to roll back quickly.
[00:11:46] Jamie Park: That's standard - model pinning and rollouts in Console. We'll demo the Console flow during the tech deep-dive.

[00:13:30] Carlos Gomez: Regarding encryption: at-rest and in-transit is mandatory, and we need customer-managed keys. Also request-level audit logs with token-level anonymization options. Are those available?
[00:13:45] Jamie Park: Yes - TLS in transit, envelope encryption at rest, KMS integration. For logs we can provide request metadata and optional redaction hooks. We'll include specifics in the security pack we send.

[00:16:05] Jonas Lee: Any obvious blockers you see for a two-week pilot?
[00:16:12] Ethan Huang: The biggest is getting SSO and sample traffic quickly; also the DPA signed so we can enable certain logging features. If those move fast, we can provision resources and run a baseline perf campaign in ~5 business days.
[00:16:30] Priya Nair: We can prioritize that on our side.

[00:18:00] Sofia Martinez: I'll coordinate dates - propose a technical deep-dive next Tuesday 2027-06-22 where Ethan will show the Console and run a live perf test with your sample payloads. Does that work?
[00:18:10] Dana Ellis: Works for us.
[00:18:12] Jamie Park: Great. I'll also send the onboarding checklist today and the security artifacts.

[00:20:00] (small crosstalk, transcript imperfect)

[00:21:30] Ethan Huang: A couple of practical items for the benchmark: please include a representative mix of short prompts and the larger context requests, expected avg tokens per call, and concurrency. If you can't share raw PII traffic, anonymized synthetic traces are fine.
[00:21:52] Priya Nair: We'll produce an anonymized qps/day and token distribution CSV.
[00:21:58] Ethan Huang: Perfect. Also, which models are you evaluating? Are you expecting Redwood to host your models or use an open model from our catalog?
[00:22:12] Dana Ellis: We're leaning to start with an open model from your catalog - we want to compare to our in-house smaller models. Potentially bring our own model later.
[00:22:22] Jamie Park: That maps to a normal pilot. We'll recommend model variants and quantization to optimize cost/latency.

[00:24:30] Carlos Gomez: Also need to confirm org-level RBAC and audit retention windows. We're likely to ask for 12 months retention for audit logs for the pilot.
[00:24:40] Sofia Martinez: We can configure retention and role-based access; there are limits on default retention we can extend via add-on.
[00:24:50] Carlos Gomez: Good to know; we'll note that for budget.

[00:27:00] Jonas Lee: On pricing - can you provide example TCO for the pilot vs projected production?
[00:27:08] Jamie Park: Yes, I'll send a pricing spreadsheet with sample run rates and Dedicated commit scenarios. We'll include a cost-per-1000-tokens and an estimated monthly bill for your qps profile.
[00:27:20] Priya Nair: Please include both hosted and Dedicated estimates, and the assumptions behind batching.

[00:29:45] Ethan Huang: Quick demo offer: during the tech deep-dive we'll walk through Console: routing policies, canary rollouts, and the observability panels with token-level cost breakdown - some of the panel labels are a little cryptic in export but we'll explain.
[00:30:00] Dana Ellis: That's great. We're particularly keen on the cost breakdowns by route and per-token.

[00:32:10] Sofia Martinez: Recap of next steps: Jamie will send onboarding + security pack; Priya will share SSO and traffic; Ethan will schedule the perf run; we target tech deep-dive on 2027-06-22.
[00:32:30] Priya Nair: Yep.
[00:32:33] Carlos Gomez: One more ask - can you share any customer references in healthcare or regulated industries?
[00:32:40] Jamie Park: We can share anonymized reference notes and some case studies; I'll include that in the email.

[00:35:00] (minor background noise)

[00:37:10] Dana Ellis: Awesome. Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[00:37:15] Ethan Huang: Just that latency will depend on model and quantization choices; sometimes switching to a quantized variant reduces cost but needs evaluation for hallucination risk. Also prep sample prompts to detect regressions.
[00:37:34] Dana Ellis: Makes sense.

[00:40:00] Jamie Park: Okay wrapping up - I'll follow up with an email that contains: onboarding checklist, SOC2/ISO artifacts, DPA template, pricing deck, and a calendar invite for 2027-06-22 tech deep-dive.
[00:40:18] Sofia Martinez: I'll own the calendar invite and internal runbook.
[00:40:25] Priya Nair: We'll aim to have SSO metadata and sample traffic by Friday.

[00:43:00] Jamie Park: Thanks everyone, appreciate your time. We'll be in touch and look forward to the pilot.
[00:43:10] Dana Ellis: Thanks all.
[00:43:15] Meeting ended.
